data.name: Breaking News Presents: Please Stand By

description.name: description
description.body:
An improvised comedy news program where YOU are the news.

Join Breaking News as they create an entire broadcast news program based on your favorite current event: you. No algorithms. No competing corporate interests. Just the blazing-hot energy of a live studio audience. Producers, grab your clipboards. Anchors, big smiles. We’re back from break in 3… 2… 1…

Fresh from their year and a half run as one of the top improv teams at Kickstand Comedy, Breaking News brings you their brand new hour long show. Featuring Thea Crowley, John Taylor, Lauren Sigler, Justin Himes, Julie Basque, and Catherine Retica!

data.name: Dirty Shirley presents Shirley's Temple

description.name: description
description.body:
Three years of Dirty Shirley. Two nights. 20 sketches. No repeats. One final, unholy offering of our greatest hits to the One True Shrimp God. Welcome to Shirley’s Temple.

Ominous events are unfolding in Portland. Have you noticed them? The skies have darkened and the dreams are coming faster now. Hard-boiled eggs un-boiling; pet snakes eating themselves like little freaks, root chakras expanding and contracting to the rhythm of the sinister pulsatile hum that issues from the Willamette. It’s clear now: Dirty Shirley is transforming and it promises to shake the very roots of civilization (in the Southeast, specifically).

20 sketches performed across two nights with no repeats. 3 years of sketch comedy condensed into one weekend. All written by Dirty Shirley and performed by Her clerics and followers: those practitioners of the accursed art of being a silly goose.

One hour to tug at your heartstrings then genitals like a feral orangutan, howling with anguish and laughter into the empty cosmos.

One night only to say goodbye to the infernal cult that crawled forth from the Coven long ago.

Email: dirtyshirleypdx@gmail.com
Instagram: @dirtyshirleypdx

Featuring the talents of:
HB Bergeson: @florencexmachina
Benny Burnett: @proud.dance.mom
Dakota Strickland: @funnydumpster
Sofia Sullivan: @subarulabubu
Alex Beeken @drinksmopwater
and special guests:
Raz Mostaghimi @razmostaghimi
Oscar Abbott @nancydrew1st

description.body:

Expect matching outfits, big beefs, and the most patient connected scene work you've ever witnessed!!!

  • Hot Dip - Jon Bolden and Dana Murphy

data.name: BIPOC Improv Jam (for BIPOC improv students & performers)

description.name: description
description.body:
*** This event is for BIPOC students & performers  to practice. All attendees are expected to participate in the jam. This is NOT a show for a general audience. Ticket is not required to participate. ****

Improv jam for BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, People of Color) performers hosted by the team Brown Sugar. The Kickstand improv jams welcome all PDX improv students and performers to get reps on stage, practice their scene work, and meet folks in the community. All levels welcome!

Every 2nd Sunday of the month.

Jams are free to attend for all, but we always welcome donations at the door to help support our programs.

Jam performers are expected to abide by Kickstand's Community Accountability Policy and Non Harassment Policy.

description.name: description
description.body:
Sketch Coven is a meetup and workshop for sketch comedians. Each month, we get together at Kickstand Comedy to read scripts in progress, give supportive feedback, and help develop a fun, vibrant sketch community here in Portland.

NOTE: This meeting will take place off site at 21ten Theatre 2110 SE 10th Ave

Click to sign up as a writer, actor, or just to observe and meet new people.

Writers bring drafts of their work for the group, including actors and acting-curious improvisers, to table read. Facilitators will provide feedback, then open discussion.

Whether you have a completed script, a rough draft, or just a loose concept you'd like to flesh out, Sketch Coven is a place to develop your sketch skills – don't be shy!

We prioritize scripts from first timers and revised drafts of sketches we've read at previous meetings. Expect to only have one script read, but feel free to bring more. We'll do our best to get through as many as we can in the time we have.

Every 4th Saturday of the month.

Suggested donation is $10 to support this and other Kickstand programs. Payment/ticket purchase is not required to attend, but please be sure to RSVP with your info.

DISCLAIMER: THIS IS NOT A SKETCH CLASS OR SHOW. While we want this to be a constructive experience for everyone, Sketch Coven doesn't teach a set curriculum. If you're looking to learn the basics of sketch writing, we recommend you take Kickstand's classes

description.body:
A late night art/food/comedy variety show where anything goes... semi-improvised, 100% chaotic

Picture this… it’s 10pm, you’re hungry, your joy has been stripped away from you by the relentlessness that is life, you go to the fridge to mainline shredded cheese straight from the bag and suddenly you’re transported to NIGHT CHEESE—an art/food/comedy variety show filled with general weirdness where anything goes.

Each episode, your hosts Aaron, Lauren, and Ghost Host are joined by a local artist who we interview about their practice and inspirations. What starts as your normal late night talk show, slowly devolves into a night of chaos. From live Tindering and hair-dyeing, to ceramics demos with cheese, every Night Cheese strictly follows no format whatsoever.

This episode's theme is ~ Witchkraft ~ Join the Night Cheese crew as we prep for spooky season, making sure everything is absolutely *perfect* by the time the Big Day™️ rolls around. We are extremely excited to be joined by Nathalie Owen FitzSimons, a Horror Scholar, Synthesist, Theatre Maker, and Mad Scientist. She’ll be performing one of her routines and dropping some mad knowledge about horror. Uncle Blade will be there to make sure we stay on track and—who knows—some surprise guests might even make an appearance. 

Don’t be a square and say that 10pm is too late for a show in Portland. Grow up.

Follow @nightcheesepdx for show updates 

----------------------------------------------------------------

“This was the most Portland thing I did while I was in town” – some guy from San Francisco at our Summerween episode back in 2018, didn’t catch his name but he was wearing a shirt with bacon and eggs on it.

“What did I just watch?” – friend from art school who came to Nothing But Jeff.

“My wife and I loved the show, can we take a pic with you?” – two extremely well-dressed people from Seattle who looked pissed off the whole show but turned out they were actually having the time of their lives at Christmas in July in December.

Comedians Max Kerwien and Alexis Bradby need to call their moms! That's why, at some point during their stand-up sets, they will have to CALL THEIR MOMS!

Comedians Max Kerwien and Alexis Bradby are touring the Pacific Northwest with their "call your mom" standup comedy sensibilities. They started performing together almost ten years ago and they call their moms often. They thought, "what if we can do standup and call our moms in one fun show?" Come enjoy their co-headlining hour of relatable standup comedy, hear them chat with their moms, and most importantly, BRING YOUR MOM!

A bit about the comedians: When Max Kerwien was diagnosed with Crohn’s Disease, he had no idea that he could turn his chronic illness into a source of comedy. 12 colonoscopies later, he’s found the funny of living with a disability. In 2026 he performed on Netflix's hit radio show "Are You Still Listening" for Sirius XM. He's performed in the Disabled List Comedy Festival and his one-man PowerPoint Presentation won "Pick of the Fringe" in the 2023 Hollywood Fringe Festival.

Check him out on instagram at @kerwien or his website maxkerwien.com

Known for her crowd-pleasing charisma and chaotic storytelling, Alexis Bradby finds the humor in how she feels vs how she's seen as a silly Black woman in America. On screen, you’ve seen Alexis bring her high energy to ABC, CBS, and Paramount+. Behind the scenes, her silly comedic writing has powered hit shows like iCarly and the Emmy-winning Tab Time. She’s been a featured performer at the Netflix Is a Joke Festival, New York Comedy Festival, and Black Women in Comedy Laff Fest.

Check her out on instagram @alexisbradby and alexisbradby.com

description.body:
This show has no material - only once in a life-time moments crafted just for you by the best of LA's Idiot Workshop. Kevin will improvise his little heart out, with the singular purpose of pleasing the audience. John Gilkey will hold him accountable and make shapes from the chaos.

Kevin arrived in Los Angeles in 2009, without training or talent, armed with only a heart of gold. Kevin didn’t begin as a show. He began as a student of John Gilkey’s Idiot Workshop. At first he was paying, and then he was not. Then he was a cast member, then he was a teacher, then like a flash of light - he was a show, directed by John Gilkey.

John Gilkey is the Founder and Creative Director of The Idiot Workshop. He has performed internationally for more than thirty-five years in circus, variety, comedy clubs, theater and television.

Kevin Krieger is the Managing Director of The Idiot Workshop. The LA Times calls him "a fixture of the LA clown scene." Kevin and John have collaborated for over a decade. 

www.theidiotworkshop.com

Press for The Idiot's shows:

“Spontaneous Theater of the absurd... lascivious, blasphemous and potentially dangerous... This could be LA’s craziest improv show”

— LA WEEKLY

“This show should simply not be missed ...transcendent...absolutely hilarious ...beautiful ...the whole thing feels like a jazz symphony made up on the spot by Duke, Miles, Coltrane and Fitzgerald. Yes, the members of Wet The Hippo are that good.”

— L.A. BETTER LEMONS

“Somewhere at the intersection of the sacred and the profane, of poetry and dire scatology, of clown and Dada, of community and exile, of fourth walls and no walls at all, lies Cruel Babes. Cruel Babes welcomes you to their family playroom for laughs, tears, and live-directed anti-theatrical chaos that is at its very least…absolutely not like anything else.”

KEITH FULTON - Filmmaker (Lost In La Mancha)

Show & Sell is the only Improv Comedy Show  where you can unload your used “Tandem Tricycle”, pick up baggies of “Slavic Hair” for only $490, or celebrate all the weird and wonderful real items from the world of Facebook Marketplace. Whether you’re buying, selling, or just browser window shopping, this comedy show/swap meet hybrid aims to unpack all the thrifted finds and kooky characters that inhabit the digital landscape of the Metaverse.

Want to be part of the action? Attendees are encouraged to bring and donate their secondhand goods in-person for a chance to see them come to life in never before seen improv gold. Later, the chosen item will be sold on Facebook Marketplace itself, with all proceeds going to Community Warehouse, a local nonprofit furniture bank that connects donated household goods directly to neighbors in need.

Show & Sell is produced by the Portland-based Improv Team Step Daddies. Starring Matt Berger, Ryan King, Sky McLeod, Katelyn Michelson, Justin Ulbrich, and special guests, this is a fresh night of Portland Comedy with vintage charm.

Wu-Tang energy meets immigrant storytelling. Bernice Ye, "The Jackie Chan of Comedy" (The Stranger Seattle), collides stand-up, comedy rap, martial arts and cinematic multimedia into one high-octane solo hour.

Wu-Tang energy meets immigrant storytelling. In Wuhan Clan Ain't Nuthin' ta Duck Wit, Bernice Ye reclaims "Wuhan" as a symbol of resilience and reinvention through razor-sharp stand-up, original comedy rap, martial arts, audience interaction, and cinematic multimedia. It's a show about identity, ambition, and building your own clan when the world doesn't hand you one. Part comedy special, part concert, and unlike anything else on the comedy circuit.

Bernice Ye is an international touring comedian, comedy rapper, and taekwondo black belt known as "The Jackie Chan of Comedy" (The Stranger), with 400K+ followers and more than 100 million views online. Born in Wuhan, China, she came to the U.S. with $1,000 and a computer science degree from Peking University, built a career as a software engineer and technical program manager at Microsoft and Hulu, then walked away from tech for the comedy stage. It was the most unhinged sequence of decisions she's ever made. It's working.

Press: Featured in the Wall Street Journal, Los Angeles Times, The Stranger, and Seattle Gay News.

Festivals and awards: New York Comedy Festival · Bergamot Comedy Festival · Best of the Fest at the Burbank Comedy Festival, Laugh After Dark, and Nate Jackson's Super Funny Comedy Festival
